title: 10 Actionable Data Governance Best Practices for E-Commerce Teams in 2026
summary: Discover 10 actionable data governance best practices tailored for e-commerce and DTC teams. Improve data quality, security, and decision-making today.
body_text: 10 Actionable Data Governance Best Practices for E-Commerce Teams in 2026 Mariam Ahmed Co-founder & CTO · January 25, 2026 In today’s competitive e-commerce market, data is the foundation of growth. From optimising ad spend on Meta and Google to preventing stockouts on Shopify, every critical decision relies on accurate, timely, and trustworthy data. For many small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) and direct-to-consumer (DTC) brands, managing information across dozens of disconnected tools often leads to chaos: conflicting revenue numbers, unreliable inventory counts, and wasted marketing budgets. This is where a strong data governance strategy transforms from a technical chore into a significant competitive advantage. Without a solid framework, you are likely navigating your business with a flawed map. Inconsistent metrics from platforms like Klaviyo, Google Analytics, and your e-commerce backend can lead to poor marketing investments and missed opportunities for customer retention. A lack of clear data ownership means that when problems arise, no one is accountable for fixing them, allowing inaccuracies to persist and erode trust across the organisation. This article moves beyond generic advice to provide a prioritised, actionable roundup of the 10 data governance best practices that deliver the most value for lean, fast-moving e-commerce teams. We will cover the practical steps needed to establish clear ownership, ensure data quality, and build a culture of confident, data-driven decision-making. We’ll also explore how an AI analyst like Menza can help operationalise these principles, turning good data into better business outcomes without requiring a large data team. You’ll get specific, no-fluff guidance to turn your data from a source of confusion into your most powerful asset for profitable growth. 1. Establish a Clear Data Governance Framework A robust data governance framework is the constitution for your company’s data. It formally defines the roles, responsibilities, policies, and standards for managing data assets across the organisation. This foundational best practice ensures every stakeholder, from marketing to operations, understands who owns what data, how it should be handled, and the quality benchmarks it must meet. For an e-commerce brand juggling data from over 800 potential sources like Shopify, Google Analytics, and Meta Ads, a clear framework is the difference between chaos and clarity. It prevents data silos, enforces consistency, and builds a foundation for reliable analytics that drive growth. A well-defined framework is a non-negotiable step in implementing effective data governance best practices. How to Implement a Data Governance Framework Start by creating a centralised document that is accessible to everyone, not just technical teams. A holistic approach often involves mastering GRC cyber security principles to ensure your framework is secure and compliant from the ground up. Conduct a Data Inventory: Begin by cataloguing every data source connected to your business. Identify where customer, sales, inventory, and marketing data originates and lives. Assign Clear Ownership: Appoint data owners and stewards for critical domains. For example, the Head of E-commerce could own “customer data,” while a marketing manager could be the steward for “ad performance data.” Document Policies and Standards: Define rules for data quality (e.g., all customer postcodes must be in the correct format), data security, and usage. Make the language clear and unambiguous. Schedule Regular Reviews: Your tech stack is not static, and neither is your data. Schedule quarterly reviews to update the framework as you add new tools or your business processes evolve. An AI analyst like Menza can help operationalise this by continuously monitoring data quality across all your integrated sources, validating that your governance policies are being followed in practice. This automated oversight is crucial for small businesses looking to scale their data analysis capabilities without a large data team. 2. Implement Data Quality Standards and Monitoring High-quality data is the fuel for reliable analytics and trustworthy business intelligence. This practice involves establishing measurable standards for data accuracy, completeness, timeliness, and consistency, then continuously monitoring against those benchmarks. Ineffective data quality is one of the quickest ways to erode trust in your numbers and derail strategic decisions. For a DTC brand managing inventory across Shopify, a 3PL, and a wholesale channel, poor data quality can lead to stockouts, overselling, and frustrated customers. A single broken integration or manual data entry error can cascade into unreliable reports, making it impossible to forecast accurately. Implementing data quality standards is a core component of any successful list of data governance best practices, ensuring insights are built on a solid foundation. How to Implement Data Quality Standards Start by focusing on your most critical data assets, those that directly impact revenue and customer experience. To truly ensure the health and reliability of your data, explore the principles of data observability , which extends beyond simple quality checks to provide a holistic view of your data ecosystem. Define Quality Metrics: For each critical data source, establish specific, measurable standards. For example, “inventory data from our 3PL must be updated every hour” or “all customer email addresses must be in a valid format.” Set Alert Thresholds: Create automated alerts that trigger when data deviates from your standards. A performance marketing team might set an alert if Meta Ads conversion tracking shows a drop of more than 20% in an hour, indicating a potential pixel failure. Document and Remediate: When a quality issue is flagged, document the root cause and the steps taken to fix it. This creates a knowledge base that helps prevent the same problems from reoccurring and improves source system reliability over time. Review and Refine: Schedule regular reviews of your quality standards. As your business introduces new products, enters new markets, or adopts new technologies, your definition of “good” data will evolve. An AI analyst like Menza operationalises this by providing 24/7 monitoring that automatically detects anomalies and quality issues humans might miss. For example, it can flag a sudden spike in ad spend that indicates a billing error or identify that inventory levels haven’t synced between Shopify and your warehouse, preventing costly operational mistakes before they impact your customers. 3. Create a Single Source of Truth (SSOT) Architecture A Single Source of Truth (SSOT) is a centralised, authoritative data repository that consolidates information from all your disparate systems. It ensures that when your teams discuss key metrics like revenue or customer acquisition cost, everyone is referencing the exact same number, derived from the same calculation. This practice is one of the most vital data governance best practices for eliminating confusion and building trust in your data. For an e-commerce brand, it is common to see conflicting revenue figures between Shopify, your accounting software, and your marketing analytics platform. An SSOT architecture resolves these discrepancies by creating one unified version of the truth. This alignment is critical for non-technical leaders who need to make strategic decisions based on reliable insights, without getting bogged down in data reconciliation debates. How to Implement an SSOT Architecture Start by identifying the most contentious or critical business metrics that different departments often debate. Focus on standardising these first to deliver immediate value and build momentum for broader data governance initiatives. The goal is to create a reliable foundation for all reporting and analysis. Identify Critical Metrics: Begin by pinpointing the 5-10 core metrics your organisation relies on, such as revenue, customer count, or conversion rate. Document Standard Definitions: For each metric, formally document the exact calculation, the authoritative data source, and the business logic. For example, define “revenue” as “gross sales minus discounts and returns, as recorded in the primary payment gateway”. Create a Data Dictionary: Develop a simple, accessible data dictionary that explains these standardised metrics in plain language. This empowers non-technical team members to understand and trust the data they use. Implement Version Control: Business logic evolves. When a metric definition changes, ensure there is a process to communicate the update to all stakeholders, so everyone is aware of the shift in calculation. An AI analyst like Menza can accelerate this process by connecting to all your sources, from Shopify to Meta Ads, and establishing consistent, unified definitions automatically. This operationalises your SSOT, ensuring that every report and analysis is built on a foundation of trusted, universally agreed-upon data. 4. Define Clear Data Ownership and Accountability Effective data governance hinges on accountability. Defining clear data ownership assigns explicit responsibility for data quality, security, and timeliness to specific individuals or teams. Without it, critical data issues fall through the cracks, leading to a culture where no one feels accountable for maintaining data integrity. This is one of the most vital data governance best practices to get right. For an e-commerce brand pulling data from marketing (Meta Ads), sales (HubSpot), and operations (Shopify), ownership prevents the “not my responsibility” problem. When the CMO owns “customer acquisition cost data” across all platforms, they are directly responsible for its accuracy. Clear accountability enables faster issue resolution because stakeholders know exactly who to contact when a metric seems off, preventing finger-pointing and delays. How to Implement Clear Data Ownership Start by linking data ownership to business functions, not just IT roles. The people who create and rely on the data most should be empowered to govern it. This approach ensures that data management decisions are practical and aligned with real-world business needs. Assign Owners to Key Data Domains: Match data owners to the teams that use the data most. For example, the Head of Operations should own “inventory and fulfilment data,” while the Finance Director owns “revenue recognition data.” Empower Owners with Authority: Give data owners the authority to set quality standards, define access rules, and establish retention policies for their domains. Their role should be formally recognised. Establish Service-Level Agreements (SLAs): Define specific performance targets for data. For instance, an SLA could state that “inventory data must be updated within one hour of a sale,” or “customer support ticket data must be synced daily by 8 am.” Integrate into Performance Reviews: Make data stewardship an official part of job responsibilities. Include data quality and governance metrics in performance reviews to reinforce its importance and recognise those who excel. An AI analyst like Menza is invaluable here, acting as a vigilant watchdog. It can be configured to send automated alerts directly to the designated data owner the moment a quality issue is detected in their domain. This ensures problems are addressed immediately by the right person, maintaining the integrity of your data-driven decision-making. 5. Implement Automated Data Integration and Pipeline Management Automated data integration is the engine that powers modern data governance. It eliminates error-prone manual data movement and brittle custom scripts, ensuring timely and reliable data availability. By automating pipelines, data from source systems like Shopify, Google Ads, and Klaviyo is continuously synchronised into a central location, ready for analysis. For an e-commerce brand operating at scale, manual data exports via spreadsheets are simply unsustainable. Automation provides near-real-time data access, which is critical for spotting issues like sudden conversion drops, stockouts, or advertising overspend before they become costly problems. It’s a foundational element of effective data governance best practices, ensuring the data being governed is fresh and accurate. How to Implement Automated Data Integration The goal is to create a resilient, hands-off system that delivers trustworthy data. This involves selecting the right tools and establishing clear processes for monitoring and maintenance, moving beyond outdated manual methods towards a more scalable, modern data stack. Prioritise Critical Data Sources: Start by automating your most vital data streams. Focus on revenue (Shopify), customer interactions (Klaviyo, Zendesk), inventory levels, and key advertising spend (Google Ads, Meta). Leverage Modern Integration Tools: Use platforms like Menza, which handle hundreds of pre-built integrations out of the box. This removes the engineering burden of building and maintaining custom connections, allowing your team to focus on insights, not infrastructure. Establish Data Freshness SLAs: Define how often data needs to be updated. Ad spend might require hourly updates for performance marketing teams, while customer data might only need a daily sync. Monitor Pipeline Health: A broken pipeline is worse than a slow one. Set up automated alerts to notify your team immediately if an integration fails, so data gaps can be quickly addressed and resolved. Document Transformation Logic: Clearly document any transformations or business logic applied to the data as it moves through the pipeline. This transparency is crucial for troubleshooting and building trust in your analytics. 6. Enforce Data Security and Compliance Standards Data security and compliance are the cornerstones of trustworthy data governance. They ensure sensitive business and customer information is shielded from unauthorised access, breaches, and misuse. For an e-commerce brand handling everything from personal details to payment information, robust security isn’t just good practice; it’s a fundamental requirement for building customer loyalty and avoiding severe legal and financial penalties. Enforcing standards like GDPR for European customers or using AES-256 encryption demonstrates a commitment to data protection. This practice involves systematically controlling data access, encrypting information, and maintaining a clear audit trail. It’s a critical component of modern data governance best practices, transforming security from an afterthought into an operational pillar that protects both your customers and your business reputation. How to Implement Data Security and Compliance Start by integrating security into your data lifecycle from day one, not as a bolt-on solution. Your goal is to create a secure-by-design environment where compliance is a natural outcome of well-organised processes. Implement the Principle of Least Privilege: Grant team members the minimum level of data access required to perform their jobs. For example, a marketing analyst needs access to ad performance data but not necessarily individual customer payment details. Encrypt Data at Rest and in Transit: Protect sensitive data by encrypting it both when it is stored in your databases (at rest) and when it is moving between systems (in transit). This makes the information unreadable to anyone without authorised keys. Maintain Detailed Audit Logs: Keep a comprehensive record of who accessed what data and when. These logs are essential for security investigations and for demonstrating compliance with regulations like SOC 2. Regularly Review and Update Access Controls: Roles change, and people move on. Schedule quarterly reviews of all user access permissions to ensure they remain appropriate and to remove access for former employees promptly. Solutions like Menza help operationalise this by offering enterprise-grade security standards, including AES-256 encryption and compliance with GDPR, SOC 2, and HIPAA. By keeping data within your own secure servers, these tools give you control while providing the analytical power you need, ensuring your security posture remains strong as you scale. 7. Establish a Data Catalog and Metadata Management System A data catalogue is an organised inventory of all your data assets, making it easy for teams to find, understand, and trust the information available. It centralises metadata, the “data about your data,” describing what each asset contains, who owns it, and how it is used. This best practice transforms data from a hidden resource into a searchable, accessible company-wide asset. For a DTC brand with data spread across Shopify, Klaviyo, and various ad platforms, a data catalogue is indispensable. It eliminates the need for employees to ask “Where can I find our customer lifetime value metric?” in a shared Slack channel. Instead, they can simply search the catalogue, discover the official data source, and trust its accuracy. This democratises data access and empowers non-technical users to make informed decisions. How to Implement a Data Catalogue The goal is to create a single source of truth for understanding your data landscape, which is a core tenet of effective data governance best practices. Start small and focus on the most critical data domains before expanding across the organisation. Start with Critical Data: Begin by cataloguing your most important data sources first, such as revenue, customer, and inventory data. Don’t try to boil the ocean on day one. Prioritise Accessibility: Ensure the catalogue is user-friendly and searchable for non-technical team members. Use plain English descriptions and avoid technical jargon wherever possible. Document Ownership and Context: For each data asset, clearly document the data owner , its purpose, and any service-level agreements (SLAs) for freshness. This builds trust and accountability. Schedule Regular Audits: Data assets evolve. Set a recurring schedule, at least quarterly, to review and update the catalogue, removing outdated assets and adding new ones to maintain its relevance and accuracy. An AI analyst like Menza provides a powerful foundation for a data catalogue by automatically connecting to and profiling over 800 sources. This centralised view gives you an instant inventory of your data assets, which you can then enrich with business context and ownership details, accelerating your metadata management efforts. 8. Adopt a Modern Data Stack and an Automation-First Approach Effective data governance doesn’t have to mean cumbersome, manual processes. A modern data stack replaces expensive, complex legacy systems with cloud-based, flexible tools designed for self-service analytics and automation. This approach fundamentally changes how your organisation interacts with data, moving away from a reliance on technical teams to build static dashboards and towards a model where anyone can get answers. For an e-commerce brand, this means the CMO can ask, “Why did our conversion rate drop last week?” in plain English and get an immediate, data-backed answer. Instead of waiting days for a report, they get insights in seconds. Adopting this modern approach is a key data governance best practice because it makes governed, high-quality data accessible and actionable for the people who need it most, ensuring decisions are based on trusted information. How to Implement a Modern, Automated Approach Begin by evaluating tools that prioritise ease of use and automation over technical complexity. The goal is to democratise data access while maintaining strong governance principles, a balance that modern AI for business intelligence tools are designed to strike. Prioritise Automation: Stop building manual weekly reports. Identify recurring questions and set up automated insights to be delivered directly to stakeholders via email or Slack. This ensures consistency and frees up valuable time. Choose Platforms for Non-Technical Users: Select tools with natural language interfaces. Platforms like Menza allow users to ask questions directly, removing the dashboard bottleneck and encouraging a culture of data-driven curiosity. Integrate Insights into Workflows: Ensure your data tools connect with your team’s communication platforms like Slack or Microsoft Teams. Proactively pushing insights to decision-makers makes data part of the daily conversation, not an afterthought. Measure Success by Questions Answered: Shift your key performance indicator from “dashboards built” to “critical business questions answered.” Success in a modern stack is defined by the speed and quality of decision-making it enables. An AI analyst automates much of this process. It can connect to all your sources, from Shopify to Meta Ads, and allow anyone on the team to query complex datasets without writing a single line of code. This not only speeds up analysis but also ensures that the answers are drawn from a single, governed source of truth. 9. Create Data-Driven Decision-Making Culture and Training A world-class data governance programme is ineffective if your team doesn’t use the data. The ultimate goal of managing data is to enable better decisions, which requires a culture where evidence consistently outweighs intuition. This practice focuses on empowering every stakeholder, from the C-suite to the front line, with the training and tools needed to think analytically. For an e-commerce brand, this means moving beyond gut-feel campaign launches or reactive inventory orders. It involves equipping the marketing team to allocate budgets based on real-time ROAS data and helping the operations team use predictive insights to prevent stockouts. Building a data-driven culture is a critical data governance best practice that transforms data from a technical asset into a strategic advantage. How to Foster a Data-Driven Culture The key is making data accessible and relevant to daily workflows, ensuring it is not siloed within a technical team. Start by integrating analytics into existing team meetings and decision-making processes, building the habit of asking, “What does the data say?” Start with Relevant Training: Focus training on the metrics that matter most to specific teams. Teach the marketing team to interpret customer acquisition cost (CAC) and lifetime value (LTV), while the finance team masters automated variance analysis. Democratise Access with User-Friendly Tools: Adopt platforms like Menza that allow non-technical users to ask complex questions in plain English. This removes the barrier of needing to know SQL or navigate complex dashboards. Celebrate Data-Driven Wins (and Losses): Publicly acknowledge when a data-informed decision leads to a positive outcome. Equally, discuss instances where data was misinterpreted; these moments are powerful learning opportunities that build collective judgment. Embed Analytics into Workflows: Instead of forcing teams to log into a separate platform, bring insights to them. A well-designed business intelligence dashboard can provide a single, accessible view of performance that informs daily activities. An AI analyst like Menza is a catalyst for this cultural shift. By providing proactive alerts and answering questions in natural language, it empowers every team member to engage with data confidently, ensuring your governance efforts translate directly into smarter, faster business decisions. 10. Monitor, Audit, and Continuously Improve Data Governance Data governance is not a set-and-forget project; it’s a living discipline that requires constant attention. This best practice transforms governance from a static document into a dynamic operational process. By continuously monitoring, auditing, and improving your framework, you ensure it remains effective and relevant as your business, technology stack, and data landscape evolve. For a DTC brand that just added a new loyalty programme and a customer service platform, this ongoing cycle is crucial. Without it, the new data sources would operate outside the established rules, quickly eroding data quality and trust. Implementing continuous improvement is a core part of effective data governance best practices, demonstrating clear ROI by tracking metrics like improved decision velocity and data accuracy. How to Implement Continuous Governance Improvement Start by embedding a review cadence into your operational rhythm, making governance a regular topic of discussion rather than an annual clean-up. This proactive approach prevents small data discrepancies from becoming major business problems. Schedule Regular Audits: Establish a fixed schedule for governance reviews. Conduct quarterly meetings with data owners to ensure policies are current and monthly audits of data quality metrics across all integrated sources. Track Governance ROI: Define and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) that showcase the value of your efforts. Track metrics like reductions in data-related errors, faster report generation times, or improved data quality scores. Create an Improvement Backlog: Treat governance gaps like software bugs. Maintain a prioritised backlog of issues to be addressed, with clear ownership and timelines for resolution. This could include updating outdated policies or fixing root causes of data quality problems. Communicate Performance: Regularly share governance performance updates with leadership. Visualising improvements in data quality or compliance helps secure ongoing buy-in and resources for your data initiatives. An AI analyst like Menza operationalises this continuous monitoring by providing 24/7 oversight of your data quality. It automatically flags anomalies and inconsistencies, generating a constant feedback loop that helps you identify patterns and proactively improve source systems before minor issues impact key business decisions. The ten data governance best practices we have explored are not just theoretical ideals; they are the practical building blocks for creating a resilient, efficient, and intelligent e-commerce or DTC business. Implementing these measures transforms data from a confusing, often untrustworthy liability into your most valuable asset. Moving beyond reactive fire-fighting, where teams constantly question reports and second-guess metrics, requires a foundational commitment. It starts with establishing a clear governance framework and defining unambiguous ownership for your critical data assets. This isn’t about adding bureaucratic layers; it’s about instilling a culture of accountability and empowering individuals to become stewards of the information they manage and use daily. The True Value of Trusted Data For growing brands, the impact of poor data governance is tangible and costly. It manifests as miscalculated inventory levels leading to stockouts, marketing campaigns targeting the wrong audience due to flawed customer segmentation, and financial forecasts built on unreliable sales figures. Each of these issues erodes profit margins, damages customer trust, and slows down growth. By contrast, mastering these best practices unlocks profound benefits: Accelerated Decision-Making: When your team trusts the data, they can make critical decisions faster and with greater confidence, from adjusting ad spend to optimising supply chains. Enhanced Operational Efficiency: A Single Source of Truth (SSOT) and automated data pipelines eliminate countless hours wasted on manual data reconciliation and error correction, freeing up your team to focus on strategic initiatives. Improved Customer Experience: High-quality, well-governed data provides a crystal-clear view of your customer, enabling personalised marketing, superior service, and products that genuinely meet their needs. Strengthened Compliance and Security: Proactive governance, robust access controls, and diligent monitoring protect your business and your customers from costly data breaches and regulatory penalties, building a reputation for reliability and trust. Your Actionable Path Forward Embarking on this path doesn’t require a complete organisational overhaul overnight. The key is to start small, build momentum, and demonstrate value quickly. Select one or two of the practices that address your most pressing pain points. Perhaps that’s establishing a data catalogue to finally document what your metrics mean, or implementing automated quality checks on your most critical sales data. As you implement these changes, remember that technology is a powerful enabler. A modern data stack, augmented by AI-powered tools, can significantly lower the barrier to entry. Platforms like Menza automate the painstaking work of data integration, quality monitoring, and analysis, making sophisticated governance and insights accessible even to non-technical teams. They act as a force multiplier, operationalising many of these best practices so you can focus on strategy rather than wrestling with spreadsheets and code. Ultimately, adopting these data governance best practices is an investment in your company’s future. It cultivates a data-driven culture where every team member is empowered to ask the right questions and trust the answers they receive. This shift moves your organisation from being data-rich and insight-poor to one that consistently leverages information to innovate, adapt, and outmanoeuvre the competition. Your data is waiting to tell you how to win; robust governance is how you learn to listen. Ready to operationalise your data governance and unlock trusted insights without the technical overhead? wafer-ai CLI: GPU Superpowers for Your Coding Agent
summary: The fastest open source LLMs for enterprise.
body_text: The Problem AI coding assistants are increasingly responsible for more and more lines of code output, and kernels are no different. But users typically run their coding agents on their local development environment or laptop, or inside a sandbox, not attached to a GPU. So you end up having to: Write the kernel optimization Sync file to GPU box Run it, profile it, sync results back Read the profiler output yourself, or paste a mess into the chat Correct your agent about its out-of-date knowledge Repeat… And if you don’t have your own always-on GPU, you’re stuck paying for idle time or waiting for the startup time of GPU providers. The Solution wafer-ai CLI is a command-line tool that gives your coding agent direct access to GPU development primitives. With the right onboarding, your agent can: 1. Query GPU documentation with citations wafer agent -t docs "What causes shared memory bank conflicts?" Instead of “Claude thinks it remembers something about 32-byte accesses,” you get answers grounded in the actual CUDA documentation, with citations you can verify. 2. Analyze performance traces wafer agent -t trace-analyze --args trace=./profile.ncu-rep "Why is this kernel slow?" Point it at an NCU report, NSYS trace, or PyTorch profiler output. The agent reads the trace data and tells you where the bottlenecks are: memory bound, compute bound, warp divergence, whatever it finds. Your agent can also query traces directly and write its own SQL: wafer tool perfetto query trace.json \ "SELECT name, dur/1e6 as ms FROM slice WHERE cat='kernel' ORDER BY dur DESC LIMIT 10" 3. Evaluate kernels on remote GPUs wafer tool eval \ --impl ./kernel.py \ --reference ./reference.py \ --test-cases ./tests.json \ --target my-gpu \ --benchmark This runs your kernel on a real GPU, checks correctness against a reference implementation, and measures speedup. Your agent can use this in a loop: write code, evaluate, see results, iterate. We support GPUMode and Kernelbench formats for specifying kernels and test cases. wafer tool eval doesn’t need a GPU on your local machine. wafer-ai handles the remote execution. Why This Matters The future of kernel development is AI-assisted. But today’s agents are flying blind: no access to real hardware, no grounding in documentation, no ability to profile and iterate. wafer-ai bridges that gap. body_text: IPG Photonics Corporation, the global leader in fiber laser technology, has won the 2026 SPIE Prism Award in the category of lasers. About the Awards Each year, the SPIE Prism Awards reflect the rapidly growing trajectory, exciting latest developments, and rich technical innovations across photonics and photonics-enabled industries. This year, the annual ceremony honored a range of established and emerging companies applying innovative and creative solutions to critical problems in areas such as cameras and imaging systems, sensors, lasers, quantum technology, XR technology, and biophotonic instruments. Finalists and winners were selected by a panel of international judges who leveraged their knowledge and acumen from across the technology commercialization and funding sectors. The distinguished judges from eight countries included government-agency representatives, commercial business executives, academic researchers, and industry leaders. About IPG Innovation The award winning product is a novel 8-kilowatt compact single-mode laser source with M2 < 1.1,which well represents the culmination of 35 years of continuous IPG laser innovation and will radically change the landscape of industrial single-mode lasers. This compact, high-power laser source delivers world leading brightness and diffraction limited quality, providing customers with higher precision for existing applications and enabling new applications across a wide range of industries. Oleg Shkurikhin, VP Laser Operations, was in attendance at the award ceremony and had this to say, “It’s an honor for us to receive this award, which reflects the spirit of IPG and our founder Valentin Gapontsev. Our goal is to develop and bring to market products that provide real value. The dedication from our people, especially Nikolai Platonov who led the R&D, is a testament to how we will continue to push the boundaries of fiber laser technology.”

title: Yaw Bediako Recognized Among The 100 Most Influential CEOs in Oncology in 2025.

body_text: Yaw Bediako is an immunologist and the CEO of Yemaachi Biotech, an Accra-based immunogenomics company focused on diversifying precision oncology. Under his leadership, Yemaachi has positioned itself as a key contributor to African cancer research by leveraging the continent’s genetic diversity to identify novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets. A landmark achievement of his tenure is the 2025 launch of the African Cancer Atlas (TACA) in partnership with Roche. This consortium aims to sequence 15,000 genomes from 7,500 African cancer patients, creating one of the world’s most comprehensive genomic datasets to address the historic underrepresentation of African populations in global drug discovery and diagnostic development. Dr. Bediako’s leadership has attracted global support, including a $25 million Cancer Grand Challenges award as part of the SAMBAI consortium to investigate cancer inequities. He has also been recognized as one of the 100 Most Influential Africans and a Bloomberg New Economy Catalyst, highlighting his role in advancing precision medicine across the continent. Through strategic partnerships with organizations such as Bio Usawa, Dr. Bediako is helping bridge the gap between genomic research and the development of locally relevant oncology solutions, ensuring that the future of precision medicine is inclusive and accessible. The 100 CEOs featured here reflect the diversity and complexity of modern oncology leadership. In 2025, some lead the world’s largest cancer institutions; others guide specialized societies or emerging innovators. What unites them is responsibility: for millions of patients, for the integrity of science, and for the future direction of cancer care globally. Source: OncoDaily

More Nakama Console Updates: More Power for Your Team
summary: New console features including fine-grained permissions, built-in Hiro integration, audit logging, and account export/import make Nakama more accessible to your entire team.
body_text: A few months ago, we revealed a completely redesigned Nakama Console with a cleaner UI and many quality-of-life improvements. We recently rolled out another round of significant updates that make the console more useful for everyone on your team, from backend engineers debugging production issues to support staff helping players. These changes came directly from speaking with our users who needed to allow team members to manage player issues without requiring deep technical knowledge. Rather than building a one-off solution, we asked ourselves: how can we make the console work better for everyone? The result is a set of enhancements that benefits the entire community. Fine-Grained Permissions The console now supports a full-fledged access control system. Create accounts with precisely scoped permissions, giving team members access only to what they need. A customer support specialist might be able to view player data and grant items, but not modify server configuration. A QA engineer could have read-only access to specific environments. This brings Nakama’s console in line with the permission models in Satori and Heroic Cloud, so you can confidently grant console access to non-developers on your team. Create accounts with precisely scoped permissions for your team. Built-in Hiro Integration Nakama now knows when Hiro is running on your server, which unlocks a new category of console functionality. Instead of digging through raw JSON in storage collections, see player state rendered in proper form views that understand your Hiro configuration. View and manage player state with native Hiro support. For example, with Hiro Inventory, you can view items as they’re meant to be displayed: names, quantities, and properties. You can grant specific items to players from a dropdown that knows what items exist in your game. For Progression, you can view a player’s unlocks and pre-conditions in a more ergonomic view. This update currently covers Inventory and Progression, with more Hiro systems coming based on demand. The goal is to make player states as accessible and actionable as game configuration. Audit Logging Every action taken through the console or the console API is now logged to a searchable audit trail. You can filter by user, resource type, or time range to see exactly who did what and when. Did someone accidentally delete a player’s inventory? Now you’ll know. This is especially valuable when multiple people are working in the console, or when you need to track down the source of an unexpected change. Searchable audit trail for all console actions. Account Export and Import We’ve improved account exporting and added the ability to import accounts across deployments. This is a big deal for debugging. Say a player reports a bug that only happens with their specific progression state. You can export their account from production, import it into your development environment on top of a test account, and reproduce the issue with their exact data. No more manually recreating complex player states. Export and import accounts across deployments for easier debugging. Open Source, Community Benefits All of these improvements are part of the open-source Nakama console. When someone has a specific need or feature request, we look for ways to benefit everyone. That’s the model we’ve followed for ten years, and it’s why sponsoring work or contributing PRs has an outsized impact. If you have workflow needs that aren’t covered, open an issue on GitHub . Your feedback shapes what we build next.

title: Anteris Announces Strategic Investment from Medtronic to Continue Advancing TAVR in $320 Million Aggregate Capital Raises
summary: Anteris Announces Strategic Investment from Medtronic to Continue Advancing TAVR in $320 Million Aggregate Capital Raises...
body_text: MINNEAPOLIS and BRISBANE, Australia, Jan. 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Anteris Technologies Global Corp. ( Anteris or the Company ) (NASDAQ: AVR , ASX: AVR) a global structural heart company committed to designing, developing, and commercializing cutting-edge medical devices to restore healthy heart function, announced today it has completed a $90 million strategic investment from Medtronic, plc (Galway, Ireland) (NASDAQ: MDT) (Medtronic), the world’s largest medical technology company. The investment closed immediately following Anteris’ underwritten offering of common stock, for a combined $320 million in gross proceeds, which supports execution of the global pivotal PARADIGM trial and advances the Company toward global commercialization of the DurAVR® Transcatheter Heart Valve (THV). Anteris and Medtronic are aligned around the belief that reshaping the Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR) market requires advancing clinical science and valve design while maintaining rigorous standards for durability, hemodynamics, and long‑term patient outcomes. “This strategic investment, along with our underwritten offering of common stock, represent an important milestone for our company. It also provides strong validation of our program from the capital markets and a major strategic innovator,” said Wayne Paterson, Anteris Vice Chairman and CEO. “The investment is one aspect of a collaboration that may expand into other strategic areas in the future. Anteris has developed a clinically important, evidence-supported product designed to improve the lives of patients with aortic stenosis as we advance toward regulatory approval.” “The Board is excited to welcome Medtronic to its stockholder community,” said John Seaberg, Chairman of the Anteris Board. “This investment aligns two organizations in their commitment to advancing valve science in a way that is disciplined and focused on long‑term patient benefit.” “Medtronic is a pioneer in TAVR innovation and evidence,” said Jorie Soskin, Vice President and General Manager of the Structural Heart business in Medtronic’s Cardiovascular portfolio. “Our investment in differentiated innovation like the DurAVR® THV technology — which has the potential to offer improved valve performance in a balloon-expandable platform — is core to our commitment to define and drive the future of TAVR, meeting the needs of more aortic stenosis patients and heart teams with a comprehensive portfolio." The Medtronic investment and the underwritten public offering of common stock position Anteris to continue to execute the global PARADIGM Trial and to continue investing in research that can transform the treatment of aortic stenosis. Wells Fargo Securities acted as sole placement agent in connection with the Medtronic investment. About the PARADIGM Trial The PARADIGM Trial is a prospective randomized controlled trial (RCT) which will evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the DurAVR® THV compared to commercially available transcatheter aortic valve replacements (TAVRs). This head-to-head study will enroll approximately 1000 patients in the ‘All Comers Randomized Cohort' with 1:1 randomization of patients who will receive either the DurAVR® THV or TAVR using commercially available and approved THVs. The PARADIGM Trial will assess non-inferiority on a primary composite endpoint of all-cause mortality, all stroke and cardiovascular hospitalization at one year post procedure. The PARADIGM Trial has commenced recruitment with the first patients enrolled and implanted during the fourth quarter of 2025. For further information, please refer to ClinicalTrials.gov (ClinicaTrials.gov ID NCT07194265). The planned expansion across other geographies includes additional cohorts. About Anteris Anteris Technologies Global Corp. (NASDAQ: AVR , ASX: AVR) is a global structural heart company committed to designing, developing, and commercializing cutting-edge medical devices to restore healthy heart function. Founded in Australia, with a significant presence in Minneapolis, USA, Anteris is a science-driven company with an experienced team of multidisciplinary professionals delivering restorative solutions to structural heart disease patients. Anteris' lead product, the DurAVR® Transcatheter Heart Valve (THV), was designed in partnership with the world's leading interventional cardiologists and cardiac surgeons to treat aortic stenosis – a potentially life-threatening condition resulting from the narrowing of the aortic valve. The balloon-expandable DurAVR® THV is the first biomimetic valve, which is shaped to mimic the performance of a healthy human aortic valve and aims to replicate normal aortic blood flow. DurAVR® THV is made using a single piece of molded ADAPT® tissue, Anteris' patented anti-calcification tissue technology. ADAPT® tissue, which is FDA-cleared, has been used clinically for over 10 years and distributed for use in over 55,000 patients worldwide. The DurAVR® THV System is comprised of the DurAVR® valve, the ADAPT® tissue, and the balloon-expandable ComASUR® Delivery System. title: Promethean ActivSuite Expands Compatibility with ChromeOS Integration
summary: ChromeOS integration delivers seamless, cross-platform access to Promethean's interactive teaching tools for educators worldwide SEATTLE, Jan. 20,…...
body_text: ChromeOS integration delivers seamless, cross-platform access to Promethean's interactive teaching tools for educators worldwide SEATTLE , Jan. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Promethean, a global education and workplace technology company and a brand of Mynd.ai (NYSE American: MYND), today announced a major expansion of its flagship Promethean ActivSuite®, which is now fully compatible with ChromeOS™ operating system. Available to educators since December 2025, the update expands access to Promethean's interactive teaching tools and supports seamless use across device‑diverse classrooms. With this enhancement, educators can now access the full Promethean ActivSuite experience directly through their Chrome interface. Using Google Admin, IT administrators can seamlessly deploy ActivSuite apps across all managed devices—including ChromeOS, Chromebox™ computing devices, and Chromebook™ notebook computers—ensuring a consistent teaching workflow regardless of device or operating system. Promethean ActivSuite is already available for macOS® operating system software and Windows® operating system and will launch for Android™ platform in late January 2026 with a release of OPS-A2. Promethean ActivSuite—featuring tools such as Whiteboard, Annotate, Timer, Spinner, and Screen Share—has long supported interactive learning on Windows and Android, and now fully extends the same experience to Chromebooks and other Chrome‑enabled devices. "For educators who operate in Chrome‑first environments, this update reflects our commitment to meeting them where they are," said Lance Solomon, Chief Product Officer at Promethean. "By extending ActivSuite to ChromeOS, we're making it easier for schools to integrate powerful teaching tools into their existing infrastructure, while expanding choice and preserving the flexibility to evolve technology ecosystems over time." For schools operating in Google‑based environments, the ChromeOS expansion complements ActivPanel® 10 paired with a Promethean Chromebox OPS, enabling an all‑in‑one, walk‑up‑and‑teach, on‑panel Chromebook experience that integrates ChromeOS‑based content with Promethean's classroom tools. Educators can also run ActivPanel from their own device—such as a Chromebook, PC, or Mac® computer—using Promethean ActivSuite, with the same seamless experience as running directly on the panel for maximum flexibility. The ChromeOS integration is available now and supports Promethean's broader strategy to deliver interoperable, platform‑agnostic solutions. Key Benefits of the ActivSuite ChromeOS Integration Cross‑platform compatibility — Seamless use across Windows, Android, and ChromeOS Enhanced classroom engagement — Interactive teaching tools accessible from nearly any device Streamlined setup — No additional software installation required Experience Promethean's ChromeOS‑Enabled Ecosystem Live: Promethean will demonstrate its full hardware and software portfolio, including Promethean ActivSuite on ChromeOS, at major international trade events from January through March 2026, highlighting flexible solutions for educators and partners. For more information, demos, or support, please contact Promethean or visit PrometheanWorld.com . title: Ardmore rolls out hydroponics for sustainability and wellbeing
summary: As Ardmore continues to align operational performance with crew wellbeing and environmental impact, we’re always looking for new and practical ways to embed innovation into our daily operations. One of our latest initiatives, the introduction of hydroponic growing systems, is a small but meaningful step in that direction. It supports several of the priorities outlined Ardmore’s Susanne Deane explores how hydroponic growing systems are enhancing crew wellbeing, sustainability, and fresh food production onboard vessels and ashore.
body_text: As Ardmore continues to align operational performance with crew wellbeing and environmental impact, we’re always looking for new and practical ways to embed innovation into our daily operations. One of our latest initiatives, the introduction of hydroponic growing systems, is a small but meaningful step in that direction. It supports several of the priorities outlined in our 2024 Sustainability Report, including crew welfare, decarbonisation, and operational resilience. With early results already exceeding expectations, this project is proving that smart, people-focused technology can deliver value at every level of the business. Hydroponics is a method of growing plants without soil, using a vertical growing system and nutrient-rich water circulated through the roots. It allows plants to grow in controlled environments, making it ideal for enclosed spaces like ships and offices where traditional gardening isn’t possible. Because it relies on stable light exposure and a self-contained water supply, it offers consistent and efficient results, unaffected by seasonal or weather-related changes. Plants are typically ready for harvest every four to six weeks. At Ardmore, we’ve used hydroponic towers to successfully grow a wide variety of herbs and vegetables. These include mint, basil, coriander, thyme, lemon balm, chives, lettuce, kale, spinach, cabbage, chillies and cherry tomatoes. The selection was made with nutritional value, versatility, and growth rate in mind, ensuring a regular supply of fresh ingredients with minimal environmental impact. Beyond sustainability, this initiative is delivering strong wellbeing benefits. Colleagues both at sea and ashore have reported lower stress levels and improved mood in areas where the towers are installed. In offices, the greenery adds a calming visual presence and encourages informal collaboration. Onboard, the system has created a sense of shared ownership, with crew members caring for individual plants and taking pride in their contributions. The result is not only a healthier diet, but a more connected and motivated team. One crew member noted that the system requires minimal set-up but brings a refreshing touch of nature into communal areas. It has become a conversation point for new crew members and visitors alike, reinforcing Ardmore’s commitment to innovation and continuous improvement. On the Ardmore Encounter, for example, each crew member is responsible for maintaining a specific plant or section of the tower. The cook uses freshly harvested produce in weekly meals, which adds a meaningful connection between the initiative and daily life on board. So far, we’ve installed hydroponic systems on three vessels: the Ardmore Encounter, Ardmore Seahawk and Ardmore Cheyenne, as well as in our Cork office innovation space. The response has been overwhelmingly positive, and the early results are encouraging. In 2026, we plan to expand this initiative across the full fleet, further integrating sustainability and wellbeing into our operating culture. Hydroponics might seem like a small step, but it represents a powerful intersection of environmental stewardship, crew care, and forward-thinking design. By investing in practical innovations that benefit both people and performance, we’re continuing to build a stronger, more resilient Ardmore, one growing tower at a time.

title: Linkhome Holdings Inc. Announces Lock-Up Extension by Principal Shareholders
summary: IRVINE, California, Jan. 21, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Linkhome Holdings Inc. (“Linkhome” or the “Company”), an AI-powered real estate technolog...
body_text: IRVINE, California, Jan. 21, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Linkhome Holdings Inc. (“Linkhome” or the “Company”), an AI-powered real estate technology company, today announced that its principal shareholders have entered into agreements with the Company to extend their lock-up restrictions until July 24, 2026. This extension follows the original six-month lock-up period established in connection with the Company’s initial public offering. The principal shareholders participating in the lock-up extension collectively hold approximately 8.07 million shares of the Company’s issued and outstanding common stock. Pursuant to the terms of the lock-up agreements, these shareholders are prohibited from, directly or indirectly, selling, transferring, or otherwise disposing of the Company’s common stock, or any securities exercisable for, exchangeable for, or convertible into common stock, without the Company’s prior written consent, until July 24, 2026. This lock-up extension reflects the continued long-term confidence and support of the Company’s founder, principal shareholders, and management team as Linkhome executes on its strategic initiatives and advances its growth across key real estate and financial technology markets. “We are grateful to our principal shareholders for their ongoing support and shared commitment to Linkhome’s long-term vision,” said Bill Qin, Chief Executive Officer of Linkhome Holdings Inc. “This voluntary lock-up extension provides a strong foundation as we continue to scale our AI-driven real estate platform and work to deliver sustainable value to our shareholders.” About Linkhome Holdings Inc. Linkhome Holdings Inc. is an AI-driven real estate technology company focused on transforming the way people search for, purchase, and finance homes. Through its proprietary artificial intelligence platform, Linkhome integrates real estate search, transaction services, and financial technology solutions to enhance efficiency, transparency, and accessibility across residential real estate markets. The Company is committed to leveraging advanced technology to create long-term value for consumers, partners, and shareholders.
